title: Kettlebell Windmill
summary: A side hinge with a bell held overhead, for the obliques and shoulder stability.

muscles.why: Library rating 0.8 for obliques (main mover): each working set adds 0.8 of a set to the weekly obliques total.
Library rating 0.4 for glutes (helper): each working set adds 0.4 of a set to the weekly glutes total.
Library rating 0.3 for front delts (minor): each working set adds 0.3 of a set to the weekly front delts total.
Library rating 0.3 for hamstrings (minor): each working set adds 0.3 of a set to the weekly hamstrings total.
Library rating 0.2 for abs: below the counting floor, so it adds nothing to the weekly abs total.

setup.text: Press a bell overhead and turn your feet away from it.
Push your hip out and hinge sideways, sliding your free hand down your leg.
Return to standing, keeping your arm vertical.

form_cues.cue: Hinge sideways down the other leg
Keep your eyes on the bell and your arm locked.

mistakes.text: Bending the elbow of the top arm.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train comfortably.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: Both sides together, Easier to learn, Doesn't finish overhead.
Swap sheet: More stable, Both sides together, Less systemic fatigue.
